# Microsoft Ignite 2026: Building Windows for the next era of work


Written By


- [Pavan Davuluri, Executive Vice President, Windows + Devices](https://blogs.windows.com/windowsexperience/author/pdavuluri/)


published


November 17, 2026


Every major shift in computing has changed what people can do at work, and


Windows has been at the center.


Today, it runs


critical work


inside your organizations


, on over a billion devices across the world


.


That


is a privilege and


a responsibility


.


I


t’s


why,


above all else


,


we’re


moving faster than ever


on


security


so you can build on a foundation of trust and lead in the era of Hybrid Intelligence


.


Agents are the next shift


in computing


.


Over the past year, organizations have moved AI from pilots into daily work, and agents are now taking on tasks across apps, files


,


and systems. In conversations with technology leaders, the questions


they’re


asking


have


evolved


. They


are past debating whether to adopt AI


. They


are


turning to agents and


want to know how to run


them


securely, and how to scale outcomes without cost


or


risk growing faster than value.


Today at Ignite, we announced:


- **A trusted, secure, and more resilient foundation.** The Windows endpoint security platform and Windows administrator protection are now generally available, Windows baseline protection is in preview, and Windows Autopatch customers deploy updates over 40% faster than with on-premises management.


- **The most secure platform for agents.** New containment capabilities in Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), which OpenAI and Meta are already building on, and Windows 365 for Agents, now eligible for Copilot Credits.


- **Hybrid Intelligence at work.** GitHub Copilot Fusion can now route coding work to local models on developer PCs, in preview, and local context, actions and models are coming soon to Copilot on Copilot+ PCs.


- **One estate, from the PC to Azure built as connected AI infrastructure.** Direct Stream for Windows 365, and Windows Server 2028 in public preview, with Microsoft Foundry and support for new AI hardware from AMD and NVIDIA.


## **A trusted, secure, and more resilient foundation**


Critical work happens on Windows, and staying protected while threats evolve has never been more important. That starts with a trusted, secure, and more resilient Windows foundation. We are making investments to harden the platform, make it easier to protect and manage devices, and keep them current.


Historically, some security protections ran in the Windows kernel, where one failure could affect the entire device. In 2024, we started working with our security partners on a more resilient approach. Today, the Windows endpoint security platform is


[generally available](https://aka.ms/WESPblog) . It lets security providers move critical protections from kernel mode to user mode, making Windows more resilient while preserving the protection customers expect. We are deeply grateful to the ecosystem partners who have built on the platform with us, including Bitdefender, CrowdStrike, ESET, SentinelOne, Sophos, Trellix and TrendAI.


We’re also making device security easier to verify. Windows baseline protection,


[now in preview](https://aka.ms/WBPblog) in the Windows Insider Program, brings foundational protections like secure boot, virtualization-based security and memory integrity together into one verifiable security state. People get better visibility into the security posture of their PC, and IT gets a clear yes-or-no answer for every device in the fleet. Application developers can use baseline protection to verify that the devices running their applications meet their security requirements. The baseline will continue to evolve as we raise the bar in security.


We are proud to be collaborating with partners from across the ecosystem to see how Windows baseline protection helps meet their needs.


We’re also making it easier to protect your devices from the risks that come with elevated privilege. With Windows administrator protection, now generally available, IT can enable local administrators to run with standard user privileges by default. When a task needs administrator rights, Windows Hello verifies the user and grants those rights to that task alone. When the task ends, so do the elevated privileges, and the risk that came with them.


The same AI that’s helping organizations scale is also helping attackers move faster. Our latest


[Microsoft Digital Defense Report](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/corporate-responsibility/topics/cybersecurity/reports/microsoft-digital-defense-report/) found that weaponizing a vulnerability, which once took expert skills, now takes just one prompt. New vulnerabilities across the industry are on track to double this year. We’re using AI to stay ahead.


[MDASH](https://blogs.windows.com/windowsexperience/2026/07/09/evolving-windows-vulnerability-management-to-meet-the-speed-of-ai-powered-discovery/) , Microsoft Security’s multi-model agentic scanning harness, now scans Windows code at a scale we’ve never had before, finding vulnerabilities earlier and fixing them faster. In October alone, we shipped fixes for more than 1,100 vulnerabilities, more than in all of 2025. Those fixes only protect your employees once they reach your devices.


Our fastest customers deploy security updates to more than two-thirds of their devices within a week. Windows Autopatch helps more organizations move at that speed: on average, Autopatch customers deploy updates over 40% faster than customers using on-premises management, and usage has grown more than 50% in the last year, to over 150 million enrolled devices. Autopatch now also gives IT more control over updates, better visibility into the features they include and fewer interruptions, with one reboot a month.


The same management principles now apply to apps. With Microsoft Intune Enterprise App Management, IT can deploy and manage apps at scale and can now preview automatic updates not just for the applications they deploy, but the applications people install themselves, with the same controls and deadlines they know from Windows Autopatch.


Windows is also standardizing on declarative management, so devices keep themselves in the state IT defines. Policies such as Wi-Fi and VPN apply, within minutes and stay protected from drift, even when a device is offline.


All of this builds on the improvements we’ve made to


[Windows quality](https://blogs.windows.com/windows-insider/2026/03/20/our-commitment-to-windows-quality/) throughout the year, across performance, reliability and craft.


[Learn more about Windows security and management at Ignite.](https://aka.ms/WinSecurity26IgniteBlog)


## **Hybrid Intelligence on Windows**


The same trusted foundation that applies to your employees extends to AI and agents on Windows.


When an agent acts on your behalf, you need to know what it can access and what it does. That’s where Hybrid Intelligence begins. Hybrid Intelligence on Windows brings together a secure agent platform and intelligent model routing across a broad range of Windows PCs powered by capable silicon.


Hybrid Intelligence uses the right model and compute for each task, on the device or in the cloud. The result is AI that’s secure by design, smarter about token spend, and more useful every day.


### **Building Windows to be the most secure platform for agents**


Agents bring big productivity gains, and because they can work across files, networks and apps, they also bring new security risks. Customers shouldn’t have to choose between giving agents free rein and blocking them entirely. That’s why we’re building containment, identity and manageability into Windows to run and manage agents securely:


**Containment:** limit what an agent can access and do.


**Identity:** tell an agent’s activity apart from a person’s.


**Manageability:** govern access and monitor what agents do.


Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) has been generally available on Windows 11 since October. MXC gives each agent a contained environment, with policies for which files and networks it can reach, enforced by Windows at runtime. MXC works on Windows, Linux and macOS, and on Windows it’s built into the operating system, which gives organizations more control of their data and a broader range of containment options, from process and session containers to WSL containers, virtual machines and Windows 365 for Agents.


Since general availability, we’ve improved quality and made agent identity harder to tamper with. At Ignite, we’re adding:


- **Process container improvements** , in preview, which give each agent a protected workspace with clear limits on what it can talk to, which networks it can reach and how it proves its identity, reducing the risk that an agent reaches the wrong data or affects the rest of the device.


- **Learning and permissive modes** , now generally available, which let IT observe how an agent normally works with system services before enforcing restrictions, so policies roll out without breaking legitimate work.


- **Local Micro VMs,** now experiment


al, give higher-risk workloads a hardware-backed virtualized boundary, with hardware-enforced isolation.


Leading


a


gent builders


and c


ustomers


are


integrating with MXC


. OpenAI has turned MXC on by default in


Codex,


Meta is running MXC on tens of thousands of Windows devices, and more than 20 agent and app builders, including Anthropic, Box, Perplexity and


Replit


, are building on MXC.


Agent 365


governance and policies


extend to local agents,


including on


Windows, so together with Microsoft Entra, Intune, Defender and Purview, organizations can govern agents with the practices they already use.


[Learn more about agent governance on Windows.](https://blogs.windows.com/windowsdeveloper/2026/11/17/enterprise-deployment-of-governed-agents-on-windows/)


### **Windows 365 for Agents**


Some agents need a computer of their own. Windows 365 for Agents gives them secure Cloud PCs, joined to Microsoft Entra and managed in Intune like any other PC in your fleet. Agents use them the way people do. They see the screen, click, type and move data between apps, so they can work in line-of-business, browser, legacy and on-premises Windows apps, including apps without an API.


Windows 365 for Agents is available as a computer-use tool in Microsoft Copilot Studio, is coming to Microsoft Foundry in preview early next year and is now eligible for Copilot Credits, bringing it into one billing, governance and cost-management experience.


Agents can now reach on-premises apps using agent identities, in preview, and persistent agent Cloud PCs for long-running, always-on work are coming to Frontier preview. Microsoft’s own business operations team uses Windows 365 for Agents to process orders and has cut processing time by 60%.


[Learn more about Windows 365 for Agents.](https://aka.ms/W365Ignite26Blog)


### **Bringing local context, actions, and diagnostics to Copilot** **with Hybrid Intelligence**


Copilot is AI built for work, and on Windows it can do even more. Three local capabilities are coming soon to Copilot+ PCs, and they’ll make Copilot more helpful in the moments that matter most at work.


The first is


**local context** . Much of what people work on lives on their PC: the files they have open, the apps they’re using, and the current state of their device. With permission, Copilot can use that information to offer better help, bringing local context into the flow of work.


The second is


**local actions** . Helpful AI doesn’t stop at answers. Copilot will be able to take action across Windows, from working with files to helping diagnose PC issues, while the user stays in control.


The third is


**local models** . Not every task needs the cloud. Copilot will increasingly use models running right on the PC and reach to the cloud when a task calls for it, so each task runs where it makes the most sense, making token costs go further.


Here’s


what that looks like in practice. With


local file actions in Copilot


, people can ask Copilot in plain language to find, organize, move,


copy


or rename files. Tidying a cluttered


D


ownloads folder or pulling project files together takes a sentence


,


and


your employees can


spend time on


more important activities while Copilot does the


work on Windows


.


**Local PC diagnostics** brings the same simplicity to troubleshooting. Copilot can run a read-only scan of the system to help find the root cause of errors or performance issues, then explain what’s going on in clear terms. Figuring out why your Bluetooth audio isn’t working or why your network connection is slow takes a quick question instead of a support call.


These capabilities can help resolve many of the most common reasons people call IT support. Employees get time back, and IT teams spend less time on tickets and more on work that moves the business forward.


And building on the


[new Windows Search experience](https://blogs.windows.com/windows-insider/2026/10/07/from-searching-to-doing-building-a-faster-more-streamlined-windows-search/) that makes it faster to find what you need and take action, we’re also now making it seamless to move into Copilot right from that very flow, for people who choose it.


### **Bringing Hybrid Intelligence to GitHub Copilot on Windows**


Developers are some of the biggest consumers of AI tokens. GitHub Copilot Fusion routes each coding task to the right model, and it can now tap into local models like MAI Code 1.1 Flash on developer PCs powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark and


**now extending to AMD Ryzen™ AI Max Series and Ryzen™ AI Max 400 Series processors** . Hybrid Intelligence is available on the GitHub Copilot app, CLI and VS Code in preview. Several Fortune 500 companies are already piloting this experience.


We’re also working with


**Adobe** ,


**Autodesk** ,


**Dell** ,


**HP** ,


**Insight** ,


**NVIDIA** and


**PwC** in the Windows Hybrid Intelligence pilot to bring local models into their development workflows.


*“Adobe’s flagship Windows apps like Premiere and After Effects already use local AI to deliver creative value to our users. Like many leading organizations, we’re looking to optimize growing AI spend, both ours and our customers’, without giving up access to frontier capabilities. We’re excited for more ways to harness hybrid intelligence to empower our developers to run key workflows in the right place, whether that’s local or cloud.”*


— Ely Greenfield, CTO and EVP of Adobe’s Creative Products


Agent builders


like


Hermes


,


OpenClaw


,


Perplexity


,


Replit


and more


are


building local AI experiences on Windows.


Christie’s


, the fine art and luxury auction house, uses


Replit’s


agent on Windows to work with private art collection data that never leaves the device.


### **One estate, from the PC to Azure built as connected AI infrastructure**


Hybrid intelligence extends across your entire Windows estate. Windows connects PCs, servers and Azure as one system, with trust and intelligence spanning them all, so you can match the model and the compute to the work. That makes your PCs and servers part of your AI infrastructure, and that infrastructure becomes how you grow your core business, scale expertise and accelerate time to market.


**PCs for every role.** For knowledge work, that’s a Copilot+ PC, many powered by Intel Core Ultra. For builders, Windows supports the broadest range of devices, from PCs powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark, like Surface Laptop Ultra, to PCs with AMD Ryzen AI Max processors. For teams that need frontier models on device, NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows brings trillion-parameter models to the deskside. AMD, Intel, NVIDIA and Qualcomm bring this portfolio to life at every tier, in devices from every major PC maker.


**Cloud PCs for everyone.** Windows 365 is the same Windows, with the same apps and the same identity, streamed from the Microsoft Cloud, and tens of thousands of organizations rely on it. Today, we’re introducing


**Direct Stream** , the streaming technology behind Windows 365 and Azure Virtual Desktop. It brings together years of work on connection reliability, speed, transport security and in-session performance to make a Cloud PC feel like a local PC. People connect within seconds, with nearly 300% improvement in connection reliability on challenging networks compared with when Windows 365 first launched. With NVIDIA, GPU-enabled Cloud PCs, coming in preview early next year, will stream full 4:4:4-equivalent color and sharper text to up to two 4K displays at 60 frames per second, with low latency and less bandwidth. Cloud PCs, including GPU-enabled configurations, can also run compatible AI models, giving developers more compute with predictable subscription costs.


That changes who Windows 365 is for. Now it’s an option for everyone in your organization, and knowledge workers can make it their everyday PC. With IT budgets tight, it can also extend the life of PCs you aren’t ready to replace, giving anyone more compute in minutes with no new hardware.


[Learn more about what’s new in Windows 365, including Windows 365 for Agents.](https://aka.ms/W365Ignite26Blog)


**Servers that run AI next to your data.** Your servers hold the mission-critical apps and data your business depends on.


[Windows Server 2028 , now in public preview](https://aka.ms/WindowsServer2028Announcement) , extends the trusted foundation to the datacenter with new security hardening, including Trusted Launch virtual machines, post-quantum cryptography and a hardened OS baseline. For the first time, endpoint teams can manage servers and PCs as one Windows fleet with Intune and Windows Autopatch, while infrastructure teams use Azure Arc.


Your servers will become token factories, built for intelligence you can own. That’s why we’re


**extending Microsoft Foundry to Windows Server 2028** and expanding hardware choice.


[AMD’s MI350P accelerator](https://www.amd.com/en/blogs/2026/more-ai-more-control-amd-instinct-mi350p-comes-to-windows.html) **will be available in preview** in the first half of 2027 for Windows Server 2025 and later, and


[NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/products/workstations/dgx-station-for-windows/) , with the GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip and up to 748 GB of coherent memory, will support Windows Server 2028 at general availability. Organizations building agents on an open model like NVIDIA Nemotron now have one path: build on a Windows PC, run on Windows Server next to their data and scale to Azure when they need more.


## **Where to start in 2027**


Every hardware decision you make in the next 12 to 18 months is an AI decision. It will shape what your teams can do, and what your tokens cost, until your next refresh. As you plan for 2027, here’s where to start:


- **Strengthen the foundation now.** Deploy updates with Windows Autopatch, turn on Windows administrator protection and evaluate Windows baseline protection.


- **Secure your agentic workflows.** Set MXC policies with Intune to control what your agents can access within your organization.


- **Start piloting Hybrid Intelligence in GitHub Copilot on Windows.** For your developers, start leveraging Copilot Fusion on Windows to route coding workflows to local models and save tokens.


- **Plan your refresh by role,** with Copilot+ PCs and Windows 365 in one plan, so every person gets the compute their work needs.


- **Bring AI to your data.** Test Windows Server 2028 in the


[Windows Insider Program for Windows Server](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/windowsinsider/for-business-getting-started-server) , or apply to the


[Windows Server TAP](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=v4j5cvGGr0GRqy180BHbRxJsFmKcaMlKrFIKRB0HjjZUOTgzNlBJT0hIWDMwSkY1Q1YzQk0zNFgxOC4u) for earlier access.


Leaders shouldn’t have to choose between moving quickly and moving carefully. That’s why we’re building Windows to be the OS for hybrid intelligence: the most secure platform for agents, an AI budget that goes further and an estate built as connected AI infrastructure, so intelligence reaches every person in your organization.


[Join me today at 2 p.m. PT for our innovation session](https://ignite.microsoft.com/en-US/sessions/1787856658187001Etji-1789751959279001dn4k?source=sessions) , where PwC’s Digital Workplace team will share how they’re deciding where AI runs across more than 360,000 devices in over 130 countries. We hope you have a great Ignite!
